---
title: "Databases, repositories, identifiers, and versions"

---

# 1. Where should my data live?

You are preparing a manuscript about past ocean temperatures using coral geochemistry. To put your new measurements in context, you have queried existing paleoclimate records through [**LiPDGraph**](https://linkedearth.graphdb.mint.isi.edu).

Your new dataset is in [**LiPD (Linked Paleo Data)**](https://lipd.net/) format. It contains geochemical measurements, age information, site locations, and the information needed to interpret those measurements. You are ready to share the dataset associated with your paper.

**Where should you preserve the published dataset so that other researchers can find and retrieve it years from now?**

Explore the five possible destinations below. For each one, make an initial decision about whether it should be your **primary long-term archive**, then reveal what it actually offers. This is a decision-making exercise, not a scored quiz.

```{=html}

    grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(100%, 19rem), 1fr));

  #pond-d4-publish .pond-d4-card { perspective: 1200px; }
  #pond-d4-publish .pond-d4-inner {
    display: grid;

    height: 100%;
  }
  #pond-d4-publish .pond-d4-card.is-flipped .pond-d4-inner {

    backface-visibility: hidden;
    -webkit-backface-visibility: hidden;
  }
  #pond-d4-publish .pond-d4-back { transform: rotateY(180deg); }

  #pond-d4-publish .pond-d4-card.is-flipped .pond-d4-front {

    font-size: 0.94rem;
    color: var(--pond-d4-muted);
  }

    border: 0;

<section id="pond-d4-publish" aria-label="Choosing where to archive a coral dataset">
  <p class="pond-d4-progress" id="pond-d4-progress" aria-live="polite">0 of 5 destinations explored</p>
  <div id="pond-d4-cards" class="pond-d4-grid"></div>
  <div class="pond-d4-summary" id="pond-d4-summary" hidden>
    <p><strong>What did you notice?</strong> An appropriate archival repository might be disciplinary (like NOAA Paleoclimatology) or general-purpose (like Zenodo). A resource such as LiPDGraph provides valuable ways to discover and query data, but is not itself the long-term archive. The same dataset can therefore have an <strong>archival home</strong> and a separate <strong>discovery/query home</strong>.</p>
  </div>
</section>

<script>
(() => {
  const root = document.getElementById('pond-d4-publish');
  if (!root || root.dataset.initialized === 'true') return;
  root.dataset.initialized = 'true';

  // These are real destinations; the coral dataset in the scenario is hypothetical.
  const destinations = [
    {
      id: 'noaa',
      name: 'NOAA Paleoclimatology',
      preview: 'Maintained by NOAA, this specialized repository provides long-term archival, discovery, and access to paleoclimate datasets contributed by researchers around the world.',
      verdict: 'Strong archival choice for this dataset',
      explanation: 'NOAA’s World Data Service for Paleoclimatology is a domain repository: its scope, contribution process, and discovery tools are designed for paleoclimate research.',
      nuance: 'NOAA accepts LiPD files in addition to its NOAA contribution template. The same service also provides searchable access to archived data—so archival and database functions can overlap.',
      url: 'https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/access/paleo-search/',
      linkLabel: 'Explore NOAA Paleoclimatology'
    },
    {
      id: 'zenodo',
      name: 'Zenodo',
      preview: 'A general-purpose research repository that accepts data and other research outputs across disciplines.',
      verdict: 'A legitimate general-purpose archive',
      explanation: 'Zenodo preserves deposited research outputs and provides persistent identifiers. It could be a suitable archival home when an appropriate domain repository is unavailable or unsuitable.',
      nuance: 'For this coral dataset, NOAA may offer more relevant disciplinary discovery and curation. General-purpose does not mean inferior; repository choice depends on the data and the research community.',
      url: 'https://zenodo.org/',
      linkLabel: 'Explore Zenodo'
    },
    {
      id: 'lipdgraph',
      name: 'LiPDGraph',
      preview: 'A knowledge graph used to search and query paleoclimate records represented in LiPD.',
      verdict: 'Valuable database, not the archival home',
      explanation: 'LiPDGraph makes it possible to work with records across studies—for example, finding coral records that meet particular scientific criteria. That makes it useful for discovery and analysis.',
      nuance: 'But it is not designed to be the long-term archival repository for the dataset. Preserve the published dataset at an appropriate archive such as NOAA, even if it is also represented in LiPDGraph.',
      url: 'https://linked.earth/FreqFun/a-query-lipd-graph/',
      linkLabel: 'See an example LiPDGraph query'
    },
    {
      id: 'github',
      name: 'GitHub',
      preview: 'A platform for collaborating on files, documenting work, and tracking changes over time.',
      verdict: 'Useful alongside an archive, not by itself',
      explanation: 'GitHub can be helpful while developing a dataset or sharing the processing workflow. Its version-control features are valuable, but a GitHub repository alone is not a dedicated long-term data archive.',
      nuance: 'GitHub can be connected to Zenodo to archive a release. That is an example of using a working platform and an archival repository together.',
      url: 'https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/archiving-a-github-repository/referencing-and-citing-content',
      linkLabel: 'How GitHub links to an archive'
    },
    {
      id: 'labsite',
      name: 'Your lab website',
      preview: 'A project page where your research team can publish descriptions, figures, and downloadable files.',
      verdict: 'Useful project page, not enough on its own',
      explanation: 'A lab website can make the dataset visible to collaborators and readers, but the site may change or disappear as a project ends or people move institutions.',
      nuance: 'Link the page to an archival record at NOAA or another suitable repository. Researchers can then find the dataset through your site without depending on it as the only copy.',
      url: '',
      linkLabel: ''
    }
  ];

  const cards = root.querySelector('#pond-d4-cards');
  const progress = root.querySelector('#pond-d4-progress');
  const summary = root.querySelector('#pond-d4-summary');
  const explored = new Set();
  const labels = { yes: 'Yes', no: 'No', unsure: 'Not sure' };

  for (const [index, destination] of destinations.entries()) {
    const article = document.createElement('article');
    article.className = 'pond-d4-card';
    article.innerHTML = `
      <div class="pond-d4-inner">
        <div class="pond-d4-face pond-d4-front">
          <div class="pond-d4-kicker">Destination ${index + 1} of ${destinations.length}</div>
          <h3>${destination.name}</h3>
          <p class="pond-d4-intro">${destination.preview}</p>
          <div class="pond-d4-spacer"></div>
          <fieldset>
            <legend>Would you use this as the main long-term archive?</legend>
            <div class="pond-d4-choices" role="group" aria-label="Archive decision for ${destination.name}">
              <button type="button" class="pond-d4-choice" data-choice="yes" aria-pressed="false">Yes</button>
              <button type="button" class="pond-d4-choice" data-choice="no" aria-pressed="false">No</button>
              <button type="button" class="pond-d4-choice" data-choice="unsure" aria-pressed="false">Not sure</button>
            </div>
          </fieldset>
          <p class="pond-d4-status" aria-live="polite">Choose an option to reveal.</p>
          <button type="button" class="pond-d4-button pond-d4-reveal" disabled>Reveal what it provides</button>
        </div>
        <div class="pond-d4-face pond-d4-back" inert>
          <div class="pond-d4-kicker">What this destination offers</div>
          <h3>${destination.name}</h3>
          <p class="pond-d4-my-answer">Your initial thought: <strong class="pond-d4-answer"></strong></p>
          <p class="pond-d4-verdict">${destination.verdict}</p>
          <p>${destination.explanation}</p>
          <p>${destination.nuance}</p>
          ${destination.url ? `<a class="pond-d4-link" href="${destination.url}" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">${destination.linkLabel}</a>` : ''}
          <div class="pond-d4-spacer"></div>
          <button type="button" class="pond-d4-button pond-d4-button-secondary pond-d4-back-button">Back to my choice</button>
        </div>
      </div>`;

    const front = article.querySelector('.pond-d4-front');
    const back = article.querySelector('.pond-d4-back');
    const reveal = article.querySelector('.pond-d4-reveal');
    const returnButton = article.querySelector('.pond-d4-back-button');
    const status = article.querySelector('.pond-d4-status');
    const answer = article.querySelector('.pond-d4-answer');
    let choice = null;

    article.querySelectorAll('[data-choice]').forEach(button => {
      button.addEventListener('click', () => {
        choice = button.dataset.choice;
        article.querySelectorAll('[data-choice]').forEach(other => {
          other.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(other === button));
        });
        status.textContent = 'Your choice is saved. Reveal to compare it with the platform’s role.';
        reveal.disabled = false;
      });
    });

    reveal.addEventListener('click', () => {
      if (choice === null) return;
      answer.textContent = labels[choice];
      front.inert = true;
      back.inert = false;
      article.classList.add('is-flipped');
      explored.add(destination.id);
      progress.textContent = `${explored.size} of ${destinations.length} destinations explored`;
      summary.hidden = explored.size !== destinations.length;
      returnButton.focus({ preventScroll: true });
    });

    returnButton.addEventListener('click', () => {
      back.inert = true;
      front.inert = false;
      article.classList.remove('is-flipped');
      reveal.focus({ preventScroll: true });
    });

    cards.appendChild(article);
  }
})();
</script>
```
